met_analysis:
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over northwest Uttar Pradesh persists and now seen between 1.5 to 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The trough in upper tropospheric westerlies now runs roughly along Long. 82°E to the north of Lat. 22°N between 5.8 to 7.6 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Gulf of Mannar & adjoining south Tamil Nadu coast now lies over southwest Bay of Bengal off south Sri Lanka coast and extends upto 3.1 km above mean sea level.
A trough in easterlies runs from the above cyclonic circulation over southwest Bay of Bengal off south Sri Lanka coast to central Bay of Bengal and extends upto 3.1 km above mean sea level tilting southwards with height.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over south Andaman Sea & neighbourhood merged with the above trough.
A fresh Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation lies over North Pakistan & adjoining Jammu at 3.1 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over East Rajasthan & neighbourhood at 0.9 km above mean sea level
The upper air cyclonic circulation over East Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood at 4.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The trough from northwest Bay of Bengal to East Uttar Pradesh across north Odisha, Jharkhand and southwest Bihar at 3.1 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
